bug_semantics: Supply-chain tag poisoning, not a logic bug on main: an attacker with a stolen maintainer PAT and the xygeni-onboarding-app-dev GitHub App private key injected a C2 implant into action.yml as a fake 'Report Scanner Telemetry' composite step, then force-moved the mutable v5 tag to that unmerged commit. Workflows using xygeni/xygeni-action@v5 between ~2026-03-03 and 2026-03-10 fetched the implant, which registered the runner to security-verify.91.214.78.178.nip.io (91.214.78.178), polled /b/q every 2–7s for 180s, eval'd commands, and exfiltrated zlib+base64 output to /b/r while skipping TLS verify and running in the background beside the real scan.
flaw_origin: Intentional CWE-506 malware written by an attacker using compromised Xygeni credentials, not an accidental coding defect. Branch protection blocked merge of PRs #46/#47/#48 into main; the attacker then pointed v5 at PR #48 commit 4bf1d4e19ad81a3e8d4063755ae0f482dd3baf12 (parent ea66a5a / v5.38.1). Identical payload had already been independently pushed as ceead6d147c867a022a4aa93a0655f0423e32770 (PR #46, 10:21–10:22 UTC) and 2d615f4e7e8d705b1ee600512e712ffcd822221d (PR #47). The published CVE is the tagged delivery of 4bf1d4e, whose action.yml added the telemetry step between scanner install and scan. Main-line action.yml never contained the implant.

reasoning: CVE-2026-31976 / GHSA-f8q5-h5qh-33mh is a published CWE-506 supply-chain compromise, not a withdrawn or false advisory. The implant never landed on main; GitHub Actions consumers were hit because mutable tag v5 was moved from legitimate v5.38.1 (ea66a5ad3128270e853f46013be382e761d930b9) to unmerged PR #48 commit 4bf1d4e19ad81a3e8d4063755ae0f482dd3baf12. That commit is the BIC of the published vulnerability: it is the smallest object the advisory, vendor report, and live v5 tag actually served, it is a single-parent first-write of the telemetry/C2 step onto ea66a5a (screenshot '1 parent ea66a5a'; parent action.yml has no such step), and it is not a move/refactor/squash of mainline code. Earlier independent writes of the identical payload (ceead6d PR #46 at 10:21 UTC, 2d615f4 PR #47) were failed merge attempts and were also GC'd; they are the same attacker campaign, not a finer reconstructable member of 4bf1d4e's commit graph. GitHub Support #4207039 later deleted the PR refs and the three commit objects, so git cannot cat-file 4bf1d4e today; parent identity is taken from the contemporaneous GitHub commit page captured while the object was still fetchable, then verified against the still-present parent tree. AI is judged only on that BIC: author is the compromised vendor GitHub App xygeni-onboarding-app-dev[bot] (Verified), subject has no AI trailers in the captured UI, and first-party attribution is stolen PAT + App key. That is human/attacker authorship, not an AI coding agent. Claude Opus 4.6 co-authored only the later README pin commit 13c6ed2 (v6.4.0), which is the advisory patched pin target and must not be inverted into the BIC. Neutralization of the live tag was deletion on 2026-03-10 plus the 2026-03-26 signed retag of v5 to ea66a5a; consumers are told to pin 13c6ed2797df7d85749864e2cbcf09c893f43b23.
